title: Police retention package and ADF veteran recruitment pathway
summary: One Nation pledges sign-on bonuses for veteran and experienced officers, accommodation allowances, on-call psychologist support and a rebuilt Police Reserve, plus an accelerated bridging course to recruit Australian Defence Force veterans into Victoria Police.
excerpt: Create a second recruitment pathway for Australian Defence Force veterans through an accelerated bridging course using Recognition of Prior Learning, with flexible arrangements where appropriate.

title: Three new Magistrates' Courts at Melton, Epping and Pakenham
summary: One Nation pledges to build three new Magistrates' Courts at Melton, Epping and Pakenham and to upgrade regional courts that need modernisation.
excerpt: Build three new Magistrates’ Courts at Melton, Epping and Pakenham — the ideal locations based on population growth and existing geographic gaps in court coverage.

title: More magistrates, double judicial registrars, fund OPP and Legal Aid
summary: One Nation would increase active magistrates toward around 170, double judicial registrars from 18 to 36, and provide additional funding to the Office of Public Prosecutions, Victoria Legal Aid, the Drug Court and the Assessment and Referral Court.
excerpt: Increase the number of active magistrates toward around 170.

title: 24/7 Bail Court within existing Magistrates' Courts
summary: One Nation would keep selected Magistrates' Court courtrooms staffed outside ordinary hours as a 24/7 Bail Court with specialist magistrates, and make every Bail Court decision a matter of public record.
excerpt: Establish a 24/7 Bail Court within the existing Magistrates’ Court infrastructure: keep selected courtrooms in select Magistrates’ Courts staffed outside ordinary hours to process bail applications.

title: Presumption against bail for repeat offenders; mandatory supervised bail
summary: One Nation would apply a presumption against bail (exceptional circumstances test) to repeat offenders and those who commit an indictable offence on bail, require published reasons when bail is granted for serious offences, publish bail data, and make electronic monitoring, curfews and weekly reporting mandatory for those bailed on listed serious offences.
excerpt: Repeat offenders, or anyone who commits an indictable offence while already on bail, will have a presumption against bail. They will face the exceptional circumstances test.

title: 90-day charge-to-trial target for serious violent charges
summary: One Nation would set a ninety-day limit from charge to trial for serious violent charges, supported by night and weekend court sittings and early certification of charges modelled on New South Wales reforms.
excerpt: A ninety-day clock on serious violent charges, from charge to trial, supported by night and weekend sittings.

title: Adult sentencing for serious child offenders; criminal age back to 10
summary: One Nation would sentence children charged with serious violent offences under the Sentencing Act 1991 as adults, and lower the minimum age of criminal responsibility from 12 back to 10.
excerpt: We will return the age of criminal responsibility to 10 years old to ensure that corrective action is taken to prevent them ending up in a life of crime.

title: Sentencing reform: community safety priority and cumulative sentences
summary: For serious violent crime, One Nation would make community safety the main sentencing priority, require cumulative sentences for multiple victims and offences on bail or parole, expand standard-sentence offences, restore Intensive Correction Orders and introduce a 'presumption of escalation' for repeat offenders.
excerpt: We will ensure that in cases that have multiple victims, sentences are served cumulatively.

title: Mandatory minimum jail for assaulting police and emergency workers
summary: One Nation pledges a mandatory minimum prison sentence for assaulting a police officer, paramedic, nurse or firefighter, under the framework used for other serious violent offences.
excerpt: Assault a police officer, paramedic, nurse or firefighter and you go to prison. A mandatory minimum sentence will apply under the same framework used for other serious violent offences.

title: Parental liability for offending by children under 16
summary: Modelled on Queensland law, One Nation would make parents liable for fines and property damage caused by children under 16 (with a defence for parents who took reasonable steps), allow courts to order parenting programs, and require parents to attend court with their child.
excerpt: Parents will be liable for the fines and property damage their children cause.

title: UK-style self-defence-in-the-home law and pepper spray trial
summary: One Nation would adopt a UK-style legal approach to self-defence against home intruders and run a controlled trial of legal access to oleoresin capsicum (pepper) spray for personal protection, with permanent disqualification for misuse.
excerpt: Conduct a tightly controlled trial of legal access to oleoresin capsicum (pepper) spray for personal protection

title: Mandatory referral of violent non-citizen offenders for visa cancellation
summary: One Nation would place a duty on Corrections Victoria and the Director of Public Prosecutions to refer every non-citizen convicted of a violent offence to the Commonwealth for visa cancellation.
excerpt: every non-citizen convicted of a violent offence must be referred to the Commonwealth for visa cancellation.

title: Abolish 10% stamp duty on home, contents and car insurance
summary: One Nation pledges to abolish the 10 per cent stamp duty charged on home, contents and car insurance premiums. The party has not published a costing.
sourceTitle: Cost of Living | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Labor still charges a 10 per cent stamp duty on home, contents and car insurance, while phasing out the same tax for business.

title: Wind back recent land tax increases on rentals and small owners
summary: One Nation would wind back recent land tax increases applied to rental properties and small property owners, rather than abolish land tax. No threshold or rate details or costing have been published.
sourceTitle: Cost of Living | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: We will wind back the increases Labor piled onto rental properties and small property owners, and we will tell you exactly what that costs.

title: Lift the payroll tax threshold for small employers
summary: One Nation pledges to lift the payroll tax threshold so more small employers are exempt. The new threshold level has not been specified.
sourceTitle: Cost of Living | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: We will lift the threshold so more small employers are taken out of the net completely, making it easier for them to hire and grow.

title: No stamp duty on new small business structures for 12 months
summary: One Nation would remove stamp duty on the establishment of new business entities for 12 months, aimed at small businesses restructuring after federal capital gains tax changes, and ease compliance burdens on small business.
excerpt: Remove stamp duty on the establishment of new business entities for a period of 12 months

title: Cut senior public service executive layer, protect frontline roles
summary: One Nation would complete the cuts recommended by the government's December 2025 public service review, targeting executive growth while not cutting police, teachers, nurses, paramedics or firefighters.
excerpt: Finish the job Labor’s own review started: cut the bureaucratic layer at the top.

title: Sunset reviews for all public entities and agencies
summary: One Nation would give relevant public bodies an expiry date so they end automatically unless Parliament votes to continue them after a public review, modelled on the Texas sunset system.
excerpt: Give every relevant body an expiry date so it automatically ends unless Parliament votes to continue it after a public review.

title: Abolish VicScreen; payroll tax exemption for screen and live production
summary: One Nation would abolish VicScreen, exempt screen and live production wages from payroll tax, make the screen rebate a legal entitlement administered by the State Revenue Office, and return VicScreen's $87.6 million cash reserve to the industry.
excerpt: Abolish VicScreen and wind up the agency.

title: $300 a year sport payment for every school-age child
summary: As part of its families package, One Nation would give every school-age child in Victoria $150 toward sport each summer and winter season ($300 per year), paid directly or as a voucher, without means-testing.
costing: One Nation estimated its families package (this and maternity measures) at $136 million, later clarified as per year; a PBO costing requested by the Liberal Party put the package at $688.7 million, including $471.3 million for sport vouchers.
sourceTitle: Cost of Living | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Every school-age child in Victoria will receive $150 toward the cost of sport for the summer season and $150 for the winter season, $300 per child per year.

title: No out-of-pocket pregnancy costs in public system; $2,000 for private care
summary: One Nation would cover residual out-of-pocket costs (such as some ultrasounds, pathology and NIPT) for pregnant women in the public hospital system, and give women choosing private maternity care a one-off $2,000 contribution.
costing: One Nation estimated its families package at $136 million, later clarified as per year; a PBO costing requested by the Liberal Party put the package at $688.7 million.
sourceTitle: Cost of Living | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Women who choose private maternity care will receive a one-off $2000 contribution toward their out-of-pocket expenses.

title: Regional healthcare guarantee including 24/7 emergency departments
summary: One Nation would guarantee minimum services in major regional hospitals, including 24/7 emergency departments and core maternity and surgical capacity, apply a Local Access Test before services are downgraded, and expand regional specialist training posts.
sourceTitle: Health and Emergency Services | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Guarantee minimum regional services, including 24/7 emergency departments and core maternity and surgical capacity in major regional hospitals.

title: Statewide interoperable electronic medical records
summary: One Nation would require linked, interoperable clinical records across Victoria's health networks so clinicians can access patient histories between services.
sourceTitle: Health and Emergency Services | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: We will require linked, interoperable clinical records so clinicians can access the history they need for safe care, use shared technology, and cut duplicated paperwork

title: Redirect administrative savings and DEI/ESG programs to frontline care
summary: One Nation would abolish standalone DEI, ESG and other non-clinical corporate programs in health services that lack a patient-care, safety or legal purpose, share corporate services statewide, and redirect savings to nurses, doctors and beds.
sourceTitle: Health and Emergency Services | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Abolish standalone DEI, ESG and other non-clinical corporate programs that cannot demonstrate a necessary patient-care, safety or legal purpose, and put the verified savings straight into frontline care.

title: Rolling fire truck replacement and replace the emergency services levy
summary: One Nation would introduce a contracted rolling fleet replacement program (FRV average fleet age seven years, CFA ten years), fit Starlink units in fire trucks, audit the Emergency Services and Volunteers Fund and replace it with a new funding mechanism.
sourceTitle: Health and Emergency Services | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Fire Rescue Victoria: maintain an average fleet age of seven years, retire trucks at fifteen, and place replacement orders at twelve years so there is never a gap.

title: Review housing fees and charges; legal time limit on approvals
summary: One Nation would review every government fee, tax and charge adding to the cost of a new home and cut those it finds unjustified, release under-used government land for housing, and put a legal time limit on planning and building approvals.
sourceTitle: Cost of Living | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Put a legal clock on planning and building approvals so applications cannot sit unanswered indefinitely.

title: Raise foreign purchaser duty on residential property
summary: One Nation would increase the foreign purchaser additional duty on residential property. The new rate has not been specified.
sourceTitle: Cost of Living | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Raise the foreign purchaser duty on residential property so Victorian buyers are not continually outbid by overseas demand.

title: Crisis beds in every region and CBD camping ban after offer of housing
summary: One Nation would fund enough crisis, transitional and temporary places so no one has to sleep rough, including modular units on surplus land and regional beds for family violence victims, and enforce no-camping rules in the CBD after outreach workers have offered a place.
excerpt: Create enough crisis, transitional, and temporary places so no one is forced to sleep rough. Fund dedicated beds in every region, including for women and children escaping family violence.

title: Land tax exemption trial for landlords leasing homes to housing providers
summary: One Nation would trial land tax exemptions for landlords who lease suitable homes, including short-stay properties, to the state or community housing providers for 12-month tenancies, and redirect short-stay levy revenue to local homelessness programs.
excerpt: Run a statewide landlord trial with land tax exemptions for willing landlords who lease suitable homes, including short-stay properties, to the state or community housing providers for 12-month tenancies.

title: Cancel the Suburban Rail Loop and redirect funds
summary: One Nation would cancel the Suburban Rail Loop, redirect the funding to other infrastructure, and publish the cost of continuing the project alongside the cost of stopping it.
excerpt: Cancel the Suburban Rail Loop and redirect funding to infrastructure that actually delivers.

title: Electrify the Melton line and complete Airport Rail
summary: One Nation pledges to electrify the Melton line, complete the Melbourne Airport Rail Link, finish regional freight and commuter track duplication, and support completion of Inland Rail.
sourceTitle: Transport and Infrastructure | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Complete the Airport Rail Link so all Victorians finally have easy and reliable access to Melbourne Airport.

title: Ongoing regional road funding and public Pothole Portal
summary: One Nation would lock in ongoing funding to clear the regional road maintenance backlog, publish the condition and funding of every major regional road, and create a public online Pothole Portal tracking repair times.
sourceTitle: Transport and Infrastructure | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Create a public Pothole Portal. Anyone will be able to report a pothole, see it appear on a live map, and track how long the government takes to fix it.

title: Replace the Victorian Curriculum with a knowledge-rich syllabus
summary: One Nation would replace the Victorian Curriculum with a sequenced, knowledge-rich syllabus prioritising literacy, numeracy, science, history and civics, and support explicit instruction and systematic phonics.
excerpt: Replace the overcrowded Victorian Curriculum with a clear, sequenced, knowledge-rich syllabus that sets out what students must learn, year by year and subject by subject.

title: School vouchers so public funding follows the student
summary: One Nation would introduce school vouchers allowing public funding to follow students to government, independent, faith-based or specialist schools, and make it easier to establish new independent and specialist schools.
excerpt: Introduce school vouchers so public funding follows the student, giving parents real choice between government, independent, faith-based and specialist schools.

title: Expand trade schools and specialist behaviour support settings
summary: One Nation would expand dedicated trade schools with pathways into apprenticeships and invest in additional specialist and behaviour support settings for students with significant needs.
excerpt: Expand dedicated trade schools that combine practical training with essential literacy and numeracy, and create direct pathways into apprenticeships and employment.

title: Ban burqas and niqabs in all Victorian schools
summary: One Nation would ban full-face veils (burqas and niqabs) in all Victorian schools, including Islamic schools.
excerpt: This ban will apply to all schools, including Islamic schools.

title: Scrap all net zero targets and subsidies
summary: One Nation would scrap all state net zero targets and subsidies and provide long-term certainty to encourage investment in upgrading coal power infrastructure.
excerpt: Scrap all net-zero targets and subsidies.

title: Cancel VNI West, Western Renewables Link and disband Western REZ
summary: One Nation would cancel the VNI West and Western Renewables Link transmission projects and other large-scale transmission projects, disband the Western Renewable Energy Zone and remove its compulsory acquisition powers.
excerpt: Cancel VNI West, WRL and other multi-billion-dollar large-scale transmission projects driven by the net-zero agenda.

title: Repeal Victoria's nuclear energy ban
summary: One Nation would repeal the Nuclear Activities (Prohibitions) Act 1983 so nuclear energy can be considered as part of the state's energy mix.
excerpt: Repeal the Nuclear Activities (Prohibitions) Act 1983.

title: Reverse gas connection ban; Victorian users get first call on local gas
summary: One Nation would reverse the ban on gas connections in new homes, give Victorian household and industrial demand first call on Victorian gas (without a rigid reservation), seek domestic prices no higher than export prices, and support offshore gas exploration.
excerpt: Reverse the ban on gas connections in new homes.

title: Ban data centres and large batteries on prime agricultural land
summary: One Nation would ban new data centres and large battery storage on prime agricultural land, require published community impact assessments and consultation before approvals near homes, and require recycled or non-drinking water for data centre cooling.
excerpt: Ban new data centres and large battery storage on prime agricultural land.

title: Ban renewables on catchment, irrigated, flood- or fire-prone land
summary: One Nation would ban industrial solar, wind, battery and transmission projects on land in domestic water catchments or that is irrigated, flood prone or bushfire prone, require full rehabilitation bonds on energy projects, and restore landholder consent for access to private land.
sourceTitle: Farming and Rural Affairs | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Ban industrial solar, wind, battery storage and transmission projects on land that is in a domestic water catchment supply area, irrigated, flood prone or bushfire prone.

title: Moratorium on waste-to-energy incinerators; block Lara and Sunbury
summary: One Nation would impose an immediate moratorium on controversial waste-to-energy incinerator projects pending review, not allow the Lara and Sunbury projects to proceed at their current sites, and restrict future facilities to industrial zones with buffers from homes, schools and farmland.
excerpt: The projects at Lara and Sunbury will not be allowed to proceed under a One Nation government, and we will work with the operators to relocate them to a more suitable site.

title: Higher illegal dumping fines plus full clean-up costs and CCTV
summary: One Nation would set illegal dumping fines at $5,000 (individual) and $100,000 (commercial) for a first offence, escalating for repeat offences with vehicle impoundment, plus full clean-up liability, and install CCTV at known dumping hotspots.
excerpt: Individual first offence: $5,000 plus the full cost of cleanup and disposal.

title: Repeal the Statewide Treaty and abolish Gellung Warl
summary: One Nation would repeal the Statewide Treaty, abolish the First Peoples' representative body Gellung Warl and end its legislated funding.
sourceTitle: Democracy and Accountability | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Scrap the Statewide Treaty entirely. Gellung Warl will be abolished and its legislated funding ended.

title: Water: restrict trading to irrigators, reinstate 1,500 GL buyback cap
summary: One Nation would restrict water trading to farmers with land to irrigate, reinstate the 1,500 gigalitre cap on water buybacks, provide full allocations at season start where storage allows, and support expanding Lake Buffalo with a pipeline to Lake Nillahcootie.
sourceTitle: Farming and Rural Affairs | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Restrict water trading to farmers who have land to irrigate, not to speculators.

title: Firearms licensing changes, amnesty and protection of duck hunting
summary: One Nation would streamline firearms licensing with longer licence periods, review firearm categories with farmers and shooters, hold a firearms amnesty and examine a voluntary buy-back, increase penalties for using a firearm in a crime, and keep duck hunting with current bag limits.
excerpt: Streamline the licensing system and move to longer licence periods to reduce unnecessary cost and bureaucracy for responsible owners.

title: YourMoney.vic.gov.au: searchable record of all government spending
summary: One Nation would build a public website recording all government expenditure and publishing the full trail of every project, including business cases, tenders, bids, contracts, variations within 30 days, invoices and payments.
sourceTitle: Democracy and Accountability | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Open the books – Build YourMoney.vic.gov.au as a searchable record of all government expenditure.

title: Royal Commissions into the Big Build and the COVID response
summary: One Nation would establish Royal Commissions into the Big Build infrastructure program (business cases, cost overruns, contract variations) and into Victoria's COVID-19 response.
sourceTitle: Democracy and Accountability | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Establish a Royal Commission into the Big Build, examining the original business cases, the cost overruns, the contract variations, the decision-making, and who was responsible.

title: Open Cabinet Act: release Cabinet papers within 100 days
summary: Within 100 days, One Nation would pass an Open Cabinet Act removing the FOI Cabinet exemption, release all withheld Cabinet papers (COVID papers first), and legislate publication of future Cabinet submissions and decisions within 30 business days.
sourceTitle: Open the Cabinet Papers | One Nation Victoria
excerpt: Within the first 100 days of a One Nation government, pass the Open Cabinet Act, repealing the Cabinet exemption in section 28 of the Freedom of Information Act
